current_findings: H_c remains one fixed-plane physical interface head and is not the root or phreatic state.
The linear analytical SWAP surrogate requires at least root-zone storage and lower-SWAP state to retain the tested hydrological memory.
Same H_c can produce different next response when root storage differs.
Same H_c and same total water can produce different next response when vertical distribution differs.
For the first linear model, a scalar affine whole-window response is exactly sufficient when bound to one committed origin state and window.
Accepted interface exchange is a mass-ledger quantity distinct from predictor response coefficients.
Internal vertical exchange is booked once per component and cancels from total SWAP mass.
Management shortage has not been introduced as physical state; later management binding must derive demand from committed root storage.
Equal integrated root-zone forcing can produce different accepted internal state and interface exchange when forcing order differs.

Forcing-order sensitivity tends toward zero in both the very slow and very fast internal-response limits; selected evidence places stronger sensitivity in the intermediate regime without claiming a global maximum.
The linear finite-window response magnitude depends on coupling-window duration and approaches total root-plus-lower storage sensitivity only in the long-window limit.
Exact substep equivalence requires preservation of the actual H_c and forcing trajectories; equal time-mean H_c is not an exact substitute for an ordered head trajectory.
Fast root-to-lower equilibration reduces the two internal storages to a one-state physical limit, but exact-continuous and implicit-Euler finite-window response formulas remain distinct.
Upward and downward exchange are represented by the same signed root/lower and lower/interface laws in the qualified linear surrogate; no direction-specific state is required.
MODFLOW-to-SWAP capillary supply is negative E_c, reaches the root zone through lower-SWAP state, and closes the complete SWAP-plus-groundwater ledger.
With only state-dependent internal vertical conductance added, E_c(H_c) is measurably non-affine over the preregistered finite head interval.
The nonlinear local finite-window response tangent depends on committed internal state, so the exact state-independent scalar tangent result from the linear oracle does not survive.
H_c can remain the sole physical fixed-plane interface head even though exact affine response sufficiency fails.
Irrigation demand can be bound to committed root storage without introducing shortage as persistent physical state.
Managed irrigation is an external root-zone input booked once; E_c remains the sole hydraulic SWAP-MODFLOW transfer.
Future irrigation demand follows accepted W_r after hydraulic redistribution and external forcing, not current-window shortage.

Real-SWAP RZM06A supports H1: at the same fixed-plane H_c, same committed time and equal integrated antecedent top forcing, two accepted internal states produce different next forcing-free whole-window bottom exchange; H_c is therefore not a complete real-SWAP state descriptor.

RZM06A H2 is NO_MATCH rather than falsified: 23/25 frozen two-interval trajectories were accepted and 171 endpoint pairs met the total-profile-water tolerance, but the largest M1 separation among those pairs was about 7.04e-7 versus the frozen 1e-4 requirement, so no H2 response probe was opened.

RZM06A H3 supports committed-origin and coupling-window dependence of the local real-SWAP response tangent. The state effect is deterministic but small relative to tangent magnitude; the window effect remains substantial after conversion to an interface-rate derivative.

RZM06A H4 confirms that accepted whole-window bottom exchange, terminal bottom flux, physical local derivative, baseline predictor u and production-facing affine coefficients have distinct semantics and provenance.
RZM06A does not require a second MODFLOW hydraulic state: the evidence remains compatible with one physical fixed-plane H_c plus SWAP-internal memory used to construct the interface response.

RZM06A2 falsifies the frozen long-window symmetric H_c pulse construction as an admissible state-preparation route: 0/56 trajectories completed their first interval; representative failures exhausted the temporal retry budget with zero accepted substeps and zero solver rejections.
RZM06A2 failures are transaction-safe: failed head-pulse trials leave committed revision, time, ledger and profile observables unchanged.
RZM06A2 does not test H2 itself; no endpoint pair was constructed and no E_c probe was opened.

RZM06A3 maps 29/56 short-window H_c perturbation points as two-sided admissible from the fresh baseline, but the preregistered selected point (deltaH=1e-5 m, dt=0.005 d) fails at the first sign reversal after 10 to 200 accepted same-sign commits.
RZM06A3 establishes that baseline local perturbation admissibility does not imply transition admissibility from an evolved committed real-SWAP state.
RZM06A3 sign-reversal failures are transaction-safe and leave the latest accepted committed origin unchanged; H2 remains unprobed.
RZM06A4 found zero two-sided admissible points in the frozen 1e-3 to 1e-1 cm/day top-forcing grid at 0.002 to 0.01 d; this is a qualified forcing-scale result and H2 was not probed.

Qualified RZM06A infrastructure already bounds the useful transition region below A4: +/-1e-4 cm/day at 0.01 d is individually baseline-admissible and +/-1e-5 cm/day is sequentially admissible in both orders.
The next H2 construction should vary forcing timing rather than forcing sign, so equal-input histories can create different redistribution ages without a reversal transition.
RZM06A5 qualified all 16 early/late equal-input trajectory pairs; no pair met the unchanged H2 water-plus-M1 gate, so H2 remained unprobed.
Without final relaxation, timing memory plateaus near |ΔW_profile|=2.8e-6 and |ΔM1|=1.43e-6 by N≈20; increasing N to 50 or 100 adds no material separation.
Fifty common zero-forcing intervals erase the A5 aggregate timing-memory signal to about 1e-14.

The current carrier executes real HeadCalc with the explicit B110 constitutive provider, but still uses the focused four-node FSI fixture geometry; node-level profile diagnostics are required before further H2 forcing experiments.
